stances.claim: The 2019 polls were peaceful and orderly relative to past exercises but suffered three insidious plagues -- vote-buying (gold), automation glitches, and overvoting -- and the most consequential is vote-buying, which has become pervasive precisely because automation has eliminated the traditional ballot-side cheating channels.
stances.confidence: asserted with named officials' corroboration (Abas, Albayalde)

stances.claim: Vote-buying is economically rational for candidates because the bribe outlay (e.g., 10,000 voters × P1,000 = P10M) is a 'pittance' compared with the hundreds of millions recoverable from 'disguised pork barrel, licensing permits and tax perks' in congressional and local races where margins are narrow.
stances.rhetorical_move: corruption-arithmetic argument (modeling the cheat as ROI)

stances.claim: Even one VCM glitch is enough to disenfranchise a citizen -- proven by Jojo Binay's eight rejections requiring personal complaint at the Comelec office -- and the many citizens without his standing and patience left polling places 'in sheer exasperation without casting their ballots,' which is 'insidious' regardless of whether the malfunction converts to fraud or wrong count (a question CJ reserves until the June 4 congressional inquiry).
stances.rhetorical_move: one-is-enough disenfranchisement principle with VIP anchor

stances.claim: Overvoting (>12 senatorial shades) on an ABS-CBN-estimated 1.2 million ballots 'could, just could' have shaken the 11th-to-14th senatorial slots given those slots are separated by only 200,000-400,000 votes -- a single electoral pestilence with arithmetic potential to flip the bottom-tier Senate results.

Voter education is the answer, with a folk-prescription specificity: voters should list their choices before going to the polling place, and the faithful should add 'Huwag kang gunggong' (Thou shall not be stupid) to 'Huwag kang pumatay' and 'Huwag kang magnakaw' -- otherwise the 3Gs (guns, goons, gold) will metastasize into 5Gs (guns, goons, gold, glitches, gunggong).

notable_anecdotes: Former VP Jojo Binay's ballot rejected eight times by a VCM and his having 'to complain personally at the Comelec office before he was able to exercise his constitutional right to vote' -- the highest-standing citizen who needed unusual recourse, used as proof that ordinary voters with less standing simply walked away disenfranchised.

Albayalde's untranslated Election Day quote -- 'Nakikita natin massive talaga 'yung vote-buying... kaliwa't kanan' -- left in code-switched Tagalog to preserve the texture of on-the-ground police observation.

The vote-buying arithmetic -- '10,000 voters with, say, P1,000 each will sum up to only P10 million, a pittance compared with the hundreds of millions that could be recovered from disguised pork barrel, licensing permits and tax perks' -- modeling corruption as recoverable ROI.

The overvoting counterfactual -- '1.2 million ballots... could, just could, have shaken the last two senatorial slots given that... the 11th to the 14th places are separated by about 200,000 to 400,000 votes only' -- the rare moment CJ flirts openly with the could-have-changed-the-result hypothetical, hedged with the doubled 'could, just could.'

The Decalogue-meme closer: amending the commandments with 'Huwag kang gunggong' ('Thou shall not be stupid') and warning of the 3Gs-to-5Gs metastasis (guns, goons, gold, glitches, gunggong) -- CJ at his most catechetical-playful.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban surveys the three insidious plagues of the 2019 elections -- vote-buying, automation glitches, and overvoting -- while crediting the polls as 'generally peaceful and orderly' compared with past cycles. Pre-election, Comelec Chair Sheriff Abas had already called vote-buying 'rampant,' and PNP Chief Oscar Albayalde observed on Election Day that 'Nakikita natin massive talaga 'yung vote-buying... kaliwa't kanan.' He argues vote-buying has become pervasive precisely because automation and indelible ink eliminated the older cheating channels -- flying voters, multiple-ballot one-hand, delayed-canvass machinations, banned preproclamation controversies -- leaving the remaining evil of bribing citizens to vote a certain way or to refrain altogether. He models the economics: bribing 10,000 voters with P1,000 each totals only P10M, a 'pittance' relative to the hundreds of millions recoverable from 'disguised pork barrel, licensing permits and tax perks' in narrow-margin local and congressional races. On glitches, even with VCM improvements over the old 'Hocus-PCOS,' there were seven-hour transmission delays (Comelec called them 'bottlenecks'), alleged preshaded ballots, and failures to read correctly-shaded ballots; DepEd counted at least 1,333 faulty VCMs and the Comelec admitted 961 of 85,769 VCMs and 1,665 of 85,960 SD cards malfunctioned. 'One glitch is enough to disenfranchise a citizen': former VP Jojo Binay's ballot was rejected eight times until he personally complained at the Comelec office, and many less-standing citizens 'just waited and waited, or worse, left the polling places in sheer exasperation without casting their ballots.' He reserves judgment on whether the glitches converted to fraud pending the June 4 congressional inquiry. On overvoting (shading more than 12 senatorial ovals invalidates a ballot), ABS-CBN's 1.2-million-ballot estimate 'could, just could, have shaken the last two senatorial slots given that... the 11th to the 14th places are separated by about 200,000 to 400,000 votes only.' His prescription is voter education with folk specificity: voters should write a list of choices to bring to the polling place, and the faithful should add 'Huwag kang gunggong' (Thou shall not be stupid) to 'Huwag kang pumatay' (Thou shall not kill) and 'Huwag kang magnakaw' (Thou shall not steal) -- otherwise the dreaded '3Gs' of manual elections will 'metastasize into the new 5Gs of automated voting: guns, goons, gold, glitches and gunggong.'
